result.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
result.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the full trade-off is reported. Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; plain adversarial training exceeds this only at about three times the clean cost. Against unbudgeted plain adversarial training on the test sets, ARAFT matches its robust R@1 at 2/255 with about ten more clean R@1 points. At 4/255, plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT still keeps its ten-point clean advantage. Developed on SuperVLAD, ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers, with no sign of gradient masking.

AI.brief_summary: 针对视觉地点识别模型在白盒对抗扰动下检索排名崩溃的问题，提出锚定式排名对抗微调（ARAFT）：在对抗 query 的最难正样本上施加 listwise rank loss，并以冻结预训练模型的干净 descriptor 为锚，在预先设定的干净精度预算下选择 checkpoint。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR/VLM 推理无直接关系，但「向冻结干净表示锚定」这一正则线索可能可供核查其能否抑制对抗或扰动式微调中的表示漂移与信息坍缩。
